Chapter Details: Status of national population, civil, address, land, business, electoral, tax and social protection registers. 44 variables in 8 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: Digital civil register eCRVS system deployed by Direcção Nacional dos Registos e Notariado, online portal civil.registos.gov.mz, rolled out to 74 conservatories and 120 posts by 2018, partially deployed nationwide per UNICEF/World Bank reports.
revision_notes: Original UNICEF evaluation-report URL returns an HTTP 400 error and could not be verified; the official e-SiRCEV portal (civil.registos.gov.mz) remains live and confirms an operational electronic civil registration and vital statistics system run by the Direcção Nacional dos Registos e Notariado. Fresh 2024 reporting confirms the system continues to be rolled out province by province and district by district rather than uniformly nationwide (interoperability with hospital birth-registration data launched in Inhambane province in July 2024, expanding coverage from 2 to 9 districts, with further national expansion planned). The UNICEF/UNEG summative evaluation of the CRVS programme (running to December 2023) confirms a 'foundational digitalized civil registration system' was established, but birth registration completeness remains around 31-32% of under-fives, indicating partial rather than full deployment. Value Code of 4 (Partially deployed) is confirmed by this evidence.
revised_comments: Mozambique operates an Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (e-SiRCEV), managed by the Direcção Nacional dos Registos e Notariado under the Ministry of Justice, Constitutional and Religious Affairs, accessible via the civil.registos.gov.mz portal. The system is being rolled out progressively across provinces and districts rather than operating uniformly nationwide: as of July 2024, interoperability between e-SiRCEV and the Hospital Data Management Module for birth registration had been launched in Inhambane province, extending digital integration from two to nine districts, with further national expansion planned. Birth registration coverage remains limited, with around a third of children under five registered as of 2022-23, reflecting partial rather than complete deployment of the digital civil register.
